record.file_problem: Repo metadata, README, and file list only; the linked paper and artifacts were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal outcomes after projecting out a weight-derived subspace, rather than testing the original difference-in-means direction.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal and capability results for spectral-subspace projection and refusal results on HarmBench, so these are included. Other listed studies concern misalignment rather than refusal and are not rows for these claim versions. File names and scripts alone are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The README reports refusal rates after projecting prompt-derived and weight-derived subspaces out of the residual stream, against random-projection controls. That is a different method aimed at V1's question. Only the AdvBench-derived subspace is close to V1's harmful-prompt direction. The top-128 weight-increment subspace is a different, high-dimensional construct.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. Refusal is sensitive to the leading increment subspace, but the projection broadly disrupts capabilities rather than preserving them. The AdvBench-derived subspace reduces refusal on held-out HarmBench prompts, and spectral anisotropy alone is not an alignment detector.
record.recipe_differences: This is a research repo with manuscript source and committed artifacts, not stated to be a replication of the original. Its refusal intervention projects out a top-128 weight-increment subspace or an AdvBench-derived subspace, rather than ablating a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The README distinguishes the spectral projection from an equal-dimensional random projection; it also reports refusal on a fixed harmful-prompt slice and on 400 HarmBench prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-3-8B Instruct, projecting out the top-128 subspace of the Base-to-Instruct weight increment cuts substring refusal from 98.4% to 14.1%. A random projection of equal dimension leaves it at 97.7%. MMLU, ARC-C and GSM8K fall substantially more than under the random projection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal is concentrated in the leading spectral subspace of the instruction-tuning weight increment, but removing that subspace broadly damages capabilities.

record.problems: Only the README and file list were available. The README omits numerical capability outcomes and does not name the model for the HarmBench result; the linked paper and artifacts were not inspected.
record.rows_left_out: No additional refusal or capability findings are stated in the README. Other reported project findings concern misalignment organisms, spectral geometry, or audits rather than the refusal behavior in these claim versions.

untested.parts: Not shown in the README: an explicit single difference-in-means direction, inducing refusal by adding the direction, and capability preservation under a single-direction ablation.
No weight-edit abliteration result is reported.
Neither jailbreak suppression of the direction nor adversarial training against its ablation is tested.
The subspace results do not compare one direction with several.
No separate harmfulness-judgment measure is reported.
The HarmBench 'transfer' is across prompt sets only, not across languages or model variants.
Refusal training methods or timing are not compared.

missing.what: How the AdvBench-derived subspace is built (difference-in-means or not, and its dimension), and which model the HarmBench result uses
Numerical MMLU, ARC-C and GSM8K scores, for baseline, spectral projection and random projection
Possible sufficiency, steering-addition or layer-ablation results for refusal

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was available. The record's 'challenges' label from capability loss was removed, because the intervention is a 128-dimensional weight-derived subspace, not V1's single direction. The emergent-misalignment results concern a different behaviour and fit no version.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report the original harmful-minus-harmless activation difference-in-means direction, a single-direction ablation, addition of the direction, or ablation at every layer and position.
No weight-edit abliteration result is reported.
No result tests whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
The subspace projection results do not establish whether refusal is carried by an affine structure, cone, or multiple directions.
No separate harmfulness-judgment measure is reported.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages is tested for the refusal direction.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.
